A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CiteGuard and retain matching methods, benchmarks, diagrams and appendix examples. The main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable in both, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CiteME evaluations, human assessments of alternative citations, LLM-judge experiments and a retrieval-versus-full-text comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds repeated-run evaluations, CiteMulti results, action ablations and iterative-retrieval experiments.

M1.justification: The retrieval actions, prompts and iterative search for additional references are retained. Section 2.3 makes exclusion of previously selected papers explicit, expanding the specification of v1's existing iterative procedure without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Alongside the retained 130-excerpt CiteME benchmark, v3 evaluates CiteMulti: 20 biomedical excerpts and 10 long, multi-citation computer-science paragraphs. This adds both a new domain and a distinct citation-attribution scenario (Section 3.2, Table 4).

E2.justification: CiteAgent and AI2 Paper Finder remain the comparison methods, and the five CiteGuard backbones are retained. CiteMulti reuses CiteAgent; no baseline is added or removed from the corresponding retained comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds controlled action-subset evaluations and explicit one-, two- and three-iteration budgets (Tables 6–9). The Paper Finder comparison also evaluates CiteGuard's top-10 candidate sets assembled from independent runs, extending v1's single-suggestion protocol (Section 5.6).

E4.justification: v3 tests the individual and combined contributions of context retrieval and snippet search, the benefit of successive retrieval iterations, and robustness to biomedical and long-paragraph inputs. Table 9 repeats the context-removal comparison from Table 7. Existing contamination examples, alternative-citation cases and the read-versus-find analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports single-run CiteME results; v3 reports five-run means with sigma in Table 2. It also adds three-run CiteMulti averages and Bayesian paired comparisons with posterior probabilities and 95% credible intervals. The 72.7% inter-annotator agreement already appeared in v1.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces single-run scores with five-run means, including GPT-4o 47.7% to 45.1% and DeepSeek-R1 65.4% to 68.1%; these are different reporting conditions. New results include CiteMulti accuracy of 34.4% versus CiteAgent's 31.1%, iterative accuracies of 60.0/70.0/75.4%, action ablations and agent top-10 scores. AI2's 55.4% top-5 entry is removed. The read/find accuracies are reassigned from 60.0/63.07 in v1 Table 4 to 63.1/60.0 in v3 Table 8, reversing the table's ranking.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 adds mathematical definitions of selected-paper and exclusion sets, a restricted searchable database, filtered search operators and the exclusion update. v1 described iteration only in prose. The original task, accuracy and agreement definitions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v3 makes CiteMulti and cross-domain/long-paragraph generalization explicit contributions, extending the abstract, introduction and conclusion beyond CiteME. It softens human-parity language to approaching human performance and changes headline accuracy/gain figures from 65.4%/12.3% to 68.1%/17%, although the 17% gain is not reconciled with Table 2.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive applicability boundaries: real writing may require users to supply context, and iterative retrieval may refuse further suggestions after valid alternatives are exhausted. It attributes weaker CiteMulti gains to possible domain and citation-style shifts and qualifies DeepSeek-R1's advantage over Kimi-K2 as statistically inconclusive. The original database-coverage and small-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the future code-release promise with a repository link, explains source-paragraph masking and exclusion of prior selections, and fills Gemini's missing token figures: 19,064.9 input and 1,449.4 output tokens. Most model sizes, costs, platforms, prompts and annotation instructions already appeared in v1's appendices.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Veri-R1, an ICLR citation-hallucination report and Gemini 2.0 Flash documentation. The research positioning remains largely unchanged; Section 6 substantially retains the related-work discussion previously in Appendix A.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: experimental setup and results become separate sections, iterative retrieval receives its own subsection, and related work, difficulty criteria, human assessment and cost reporting move into the main text. Appendices are reorganized, with accompanying language edits and expanded explanations.

P2.justification: v3 adds tables for Bayesian comparisons, CiteMulti, iteration budgets and action ablations; converts appendix budget bullets into Table 5; and consolidates the earlier judge-result tables into Table 1. Retrieval-action and reasoning-example figures move into the main text. Table 2 gains uncertainty formatting, and the Paper Finder table changes columns. The underlying diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: Repeated-run reporting and direct action ablations make the empirical support more assessable, while the corrected read/find table resolves a contradiction in v1. However, v3 introduces an unsupported 17% headline gain: Table 2 reports 45.1% versus 35.3%, a 9.8-point difference. Section 4.1 also still describes Table 2 using v1's 12.3%/65.4% figures. These central reporting inconsistencies limit the overall benefit despite the stronger experimental evidence.
